question: Find the part of the sentence that has an error: Each of the applicants (A) / have been asked (B) / to bring original documents. (C)
explanation: Each takes a singular verb: has been asked.

question: Find the part of the sentence that has an error: The auditors examined (A) / the accounts thoroughly (B) / before signing the report. (C)
Find the part of the sentence that has an error: The interviewer asked him (A) / why he wanted (B) / to join a bank? (C)
explanation: An indirect question ends with a full stop, not a question mark.

question: Find the part of the sentence that has an error: Hardly had the manager left (A) / than the customers (B) / began to complain. (C)
Find the part of the sentence that has an error: She bought (A) / many new furnitures (B) / for her flat. (C)
explanation: Furniture is uncountable and has no plural.

question: Find the part of the sentence that has an error: One of my friends (A) / are working as (B) / a probationary officer. (C)
explanation: One of + plural noun takes a singular verb.

question: Find the part of the sentence that has an error: If I was the manager, (A) / I would approve (B) / the loan immediately. (C)
Find the part of the sentence that has an error: The customer asked me (A) / where was the (B) / cash counter. (C)
explanation: Indirect questions use statement order: where the cash counter was.

question: Find the part of the sentence that has an error: Lest you should not (A) / miss the train, (B) / leave home early. (C)
Find the part of the sentence that has an error: The cashier, along with his assistants, (A) / were suspended (B) / for negligence. (C)
explanation: Along with does not change the singular subject: was.

question: Find the part of the sentence that has an error: Mathematics are (A) / my favourite subject (B) / at school. (C)
Find the part of the sentence that has an error: Of the two proposals, (A) / the first is (B) / more preferable. (C)
Find the part of the sentence that has an error: Myself and Rohan (A) / will handle (B) / the audit this week. (C)
explanation: A reflexive pronoun cannot be a subject: Rohan and I.

question: Find the part of the sentence that has an error: The officer was (A) / so busy that he (B) / could not able to attend the call. (C)
explanation: Use 'could not' or 'was not able to', not both.

question: Find the part of the sentence that has an error: He is one of the best officers (A) / who has ever worked (B) / in this branch. (C)
explanation: Who refers to plural 'officers': have worked.

question: Find the part of the sentence that has an error: The loan was sanctioned (A) / after the bank verified (B) / all the documents. (C)
Find the part of the sentence that has an error: Neither of the two candidates (A) / were selected (B) / for the post. (C)
explanation: Neither takes a singular verb: was.

question: Find the part of the sentence that has an error: Does he knows (A) / the procedure for (B) / opening a locker? (C)
explanation: Does is followed by the base form: know.

question: Find the part of the sentence that has an error: The bank has opened (A) / a new branch (B) / in the outskirt of the city. (C)
Find the part of the sentence that has an error: The jewellery that (A) / she deposited in the locker (B) / were very valuable. (C)
explanation: Jewellery is uncountable and takes a singular verb.

question: Find the part of the sentence that has an error: He did not attend (A) / the meeting yesterday (B) / because he was suffering from fever since Monday. (C)
explanation: An action continuing up to a past point takes the past perfect continuous: had been suffering.

question: Find the part of the sentence that has an error: The new manager is (A) / more stricter than (B) / the previous one. (C)
Find the part of the sentence that has an error: Ravi and Sita, (A) / who are siblings, (B) / work in the same bank. (C)
Find the part of the sentence that has an error: The poor (A) / needs our help (B) / and support. (C)
explanation: The + adjective denotes a plural class: need.

question: Find the part of the sentence that has an error: He gave me (A) / an useful piece (B) / of advice. (C)
explanation: 'Useful' begins with a 'yoo' sound: a useful.

question: Find the part of the sentence that has an error: The bank will remain closed (A) / on Monday (B) / on account of the holiday. (C)
Find the part of the sentence that has an error: Scarcely had we entered the hall (A) / when the lights (B) / went out. (C)
Find the part of the sentence that has an error: The lady who's purse (A) / was stolen (B) / filed a complaint. (C)
Find the part of the sentence that has an error: The manager ordered (A) / that the files (B) / are sent to head office. (C)
explanation: Order that takes the subjunctive: be sent.

question: Find the part of the sentence that has an error: My brother-in-laws (A) / are coming (B) / to visit us. (C)
Find the part of the sentence that has an error: For a beginner, (A) / she speaks (B) / English very good. (C)
explanation: Use the adverb 'well' to modify a verb.

question: Find the part of the sentence that has an error: The bus was late, (A) / so we had to (B) / take a taxi. (C)
Find the part of the sentence that has an error: Let you and I (A) / go to the bank (B) / before it closes. (C)
explanation: Let takes the object form: you and me.

question: Find the part of the sentence that has an error: The new trainee is (A) / not only hardworking (B) / but also an honest. (C)
explanation: Parallel structure: not only hardworking but also honest.

question: Find the part of the sentence that has an error: The childrens (A) / are playing (B) / in the park. (C)
explanation: The plural of child is children.

question: Find the part of the sentence that has an error: After years in banking, (A) / I am used to (B) / work late on Fridays. (C)
explanation: Be used to takes a gerund: working.

question: Find the part of the sentence that has an error: The audit report (A) / which you sent me (B) / were incomplete. (C)
Find the part of the sentence that has an error: The most cleverest (A) / student in the class (B) / topped the exam. (C)
Find the part of the sentence that has an error: The majority of the employees (A) / have opted for (B) / the new pension scheme. (C)
Find the part of the sentence that has an error: I have been knowing (A) / Rahul since (B) / our college days. (C)
explanation: Know is stative and not used in continuous form: have known.

question: Find the part of the sentence that has an error: The manager congratulated him (A) / for (B) / his well-deserved promotion. (C)
Find the part of the sentence that has an error: The new branch (A) / is consisted of (B) / five departments. (C)
explanation: Consist is not used in the passive: consists of.

question: Find the part of the sentence that has an error: Please return the files (A) / to me (B) / by tomorrow evening. (C)
Find the part of the sentence that has an error: The cattle is grazing (A) / in the field (B) / near the river. (C)
Find the part of the sentence that has an error: The minister announced (A) / that the new scheme (B) / will be launched on next Monday. (C)
explanation: No preposition before 'next' + day, and reported speech takes 'would'.

question: Find the part of the sentence that has an error: Bread and butter (A) / are (B) / my usual breakfast. (C)
explanation: Bread and butter as one idea takes a singular verb: is.

question: Find the part of the sentence that has an error: Not only he is intelligent (A) / but also (B) / hardworking. (C)
explanation: Not only at the start needs inversion: Not only is he.

question: Find the part of the sentence that has an error: The branch manager, as well as the clerks, (A) / is attending (B) / the training session. (C)
explanation: With 'as well as' the verb agrees with the first subject.

question: Find the part of the sentence that has an error: Excuse me, (A) / would you mind (B) / to close the window? (C)
Find the part of the sentence that has an error: Our manager was (A) / quite annoyed (B) / on me for coming late. (C)
Choose the best replacement for the capitalised part of the sentence: The officer, together with his staff, ARE ATTENDING the seminar.
explanation: Together with does not change the singular subject.

question: Choose the best replacement for the capitalised part of the sentence: She is good AT SINGING as well as dancing.
explanation: Good at is the correct usage.

question: Choose the best replacement for the capitalised part of the sentence: The guests WERE ARRIVED before the host.
explanation: Arrive is intransitive; the earlier past action takes the past perfect.

question: Choose the best replacement for the capitalised part of the sentence: IF HE WILL COME tomorrow, I will give him the cheque.
Choose the best replacement for the capitalised part of the sentence: He walked carefully LEST HE WOULD fall on the icy road.
Choose the best replacement for the capitalised part of the sentence: The sum and substance of his speech WERE that we should work harder.
explanation: Sum and substance is one idea and takes a singular verb.

question: Choose the best replacement for the capitalised part of the sentence: He IS WORKING in this bank for ten years.
explanation: Action continuing from past to present: present perfect continuous.

question: Choose the best replacement for the capitalised part of the sentence: Seldom DO WE SEE such dedication in young officers.
explanation: A negative adverb at the start needs inversion.

question: Choose the best replacement for the capitalised part of the sentence: THE ENGLISH ARE known for their love of tea.
Choose the best replacement for the capitalised part of the sentence: The doctor advised him TO NOT TO SMOKE.
Choose the best replacement for the capitalised part of the sentence: She COULD NOT BUT HELP laughing at the joke.
explanation: Could not help + gerund, or could not but + base verb.

question: Choose the best replacement for the capitalised part of the sentence: Each of the girls HAS SUBMITTED her assignment.
Choose the best replacement for the capitalised part of the sentence: He is TOO MUCH INTELLIGENT to make such a mistake.
Choose the best replacement for the capitalised part of the sentence: The manager made him TO WORK late on Saturday.
explanation: Make + object takes a bare infinitive.

question: Choose the best replacement for the capitalised part of the sentence: Many a student HAS FAILED this paper.
explanation: Many a takes a singular verb.

question: Choose the best replacement for the capitalised part of the sentence: She has LESS FRIENDS than her sister.
Choose the best replacement for the capitalised part of the sentence: Ravi is THE TALLEST OF THE TWO brothers.
options: the more tall of the two
explanation: Use the comparative when comparing two.

question: Choose the best replacement for the capitalised part of the sentence: By next March, she WILL HAVE COMPLETED ten years in service.
explanation: Future perfect for an action completed before a future time.

question: Choose the best replacement for the capitalised part of the sentence: He DID NOT HAVE NO MONEY to pay the fee.
Choose the best replacement for the capitalised part of the sentence: WHILE CROSSING the road, a car hit him.
options: While crossing the road by him
While he was crossing the road
explanation: Avoid dangling participles; name the doer.

question: Choose the best replacement for the capitalised part of the sentence: The cheque was issued ON YESTERDAY.
Choose the best replacement for the capitalised part of the sentence: She WAS BORN IN 12th May 1995.
Choose the best replacement for the capitalised part of the sentence: He AVAILED the opportunity.
explanation: Avail is used reflexively: avail oneself of.

question: Choose the best replacement for the capitalised part of the sentence: My uncle, WHOM I THOUGHT was abroad, visited us yesterday.
explanation: The pronoun is the subject of 'was': who.

question: Choose the best replacement for the capitalised part of the sentence: Not a single word WERE SPOKEN by the accused.
explanation: Not a single + singular noun takes a singular verb.

question: Choose the best replacement for the capitalised part of the sentence: The meeting WAS POSTPONED FOR next week.
Choose the best replacement for the capitalised part of the sentence: Unless you WORK HARD, you will not succeed.
Choose the best replacement for the capitalised part of the sentence: THE TWO FIRST chapters of the book are boring.
explanation: Ordinal comes before cardinal: the first two.

question: Choose the best replacement for the capitalised part of the sentence: He is ENTITLED FOR a pension after retirement.
Choose the best replacement for the capitalised part of the sentence: She did not come to office BECAUSE OF SHE WAS ill.
explanation: Because introduces a clause; because of takes a noun.

question: Fill in the blank: The bank has introduced a new scheme _____ encourage savings among rural women.
Fill in the blank: He was fined _____ violating traffic rules.
Fill in the blank: _____ you leave now, you will miss the last bus.
Fill in the blank: The applicant was _____ for the post because he lacked experience.
Fill in the blank: She has been living in Mumbai _____ 2018.
explanation: Since with a point of time.

question: Fill in the blank: The RBI _____ the repo rate by 25 basis points last week.
explanation: Past time marker takes the simple past.

question: Fill in the blank: He is very _____ about his work and never misses a deadline.
Fill in the blank: The minister refused to comment _____ the issue.
Fill in the blank: By the time the police arrived, the thieves _____.
explanation: Past perfect for the earlier of two past actions.

question: Fill in the blank: The project was a success _____ the initial setbacks.
Fill in the blank: The company is short _____ funds this quarter.
Fill in the blank: The customer lodged a _____ against the rude behaviour of the staff.
Fill in the blank: Keep the receipt _____ you need it later.
explanation: In case = as a precaution against.

question: Fill in the blank: He talks as if he _____ the owner of the company.
Fill in the blank: The thief was caught red-handed and _____ to the police.
Fill in the blank: The interest rate on savings accounts varies _____ bank to bank.
Fill in the blank: The quality of these products _____ improved remarkably.
Fill in the blank: The new policy will come _____ effect from April 1.
Fill in the blank: She was so tired _____ she fell asleep at her desk.
Fill in the blank: The revised service charges are applicable _____ all savings account holders.
Fill in the blank: The bank _____ its customers of any change in charges in advance.
Fill in the blank: The ship sank _____ the efforts of the crew to save it.
Fill in the blank: The documents must be submitted _____ the end of this month.
Fill in the blank: He was _____ to the post of Deputy General Manager.
explanation: Passive voice needs the past participle.

question: Fill in the blank: _____ of the two answers is correct; both are wrong.
Fill in the blank: Make sure you switch _____ the lights before leaving the office.
Fill in the blank: The economy is expected to grow _____ a rate of 7 percent.
Fill in the blank: Had I known about the strike, I _____ the trip.
explanation: Inverted third conditional takes would have + past participle.

question: Fill in the blank: The old building was _____ to make way for a shopping mall.
Fill in the blank: He is _____ honest man that everyone trusts him.
Fill in the blank: The accountant could not account _____ the missing cash.
Fill in the blank: She has a great _____ for music.
Fill in the blank: He walked _____ the road to reach the bus stop on the other side.
explanation: Across = from one side to the other.

question: Fill in the blank: Every employee _____ to wear the ID card inside the premises.
Fill in the blank: The bridge, _____ was built in 1950, needs urgent repairs.
Fill in the blank: He has not received his salary _____.
explanation: Yet is used in negative sentences.

question: Fill in the blank: I would rather stay at home _____ go to the party.
Fill in the blank: The committee is looking _____ the complaint and will report next week.
Fill in the blank: There is hardly _____ milk left in the fridge.
Fill in the blank: The loan amount will be credited to your account _____ two working days.
explanation: Within = before the end of a period.

To manage to live on a limited income

question: What is the meaning of the idiom "To leave no stone unturned"?

A person who is very lucky
A person who feels uncomfortable in unfamiliar surroundings

question: What is the meaning of the idiom "To be all ears"?
What is the meaning of the idiom "To take the bull by the horns"?

question: What is the meaning of the idiom "To see eye to eye"?
What is the meaning of the idiom "To bury the hatchet"?

question: What is the meaning of the idiom "In hot water"?
What is the meaning of the idiom "To kill two birds with one stone"?

question: What is the meaning of the idiom "To nip in the bud"?

question: What is the meaning of the idiom "To face the music"?

question: What is the meaning of the idiom "To hit the sack"?
What is the meaning of the idiom "A storm in a teacup"?

question: What is the meaning of the idiom "To play second fiddle"?

question: What is the meaning of the idiom "A feather in one's cap"?
options: An achievement one can be proud of

question: What is the meaning of the idiom "To get the sack"?

question: What is the meaning of the idiom "To keep the wolf from the door"?

To have just enough money to avoid hunger and poverty

question: What is the meaning of the idiom "By leaps and bounds"?
What is the meaning of the idiom "To sit on the fence"?

question: What is the meaning of the idiom "Hand in glove"?
options: In close association, especially in wrongdoing

Rearrange the sentences P, Q, R, S to form a meaningful paragraph: P. After retiring from the bank, he finally rented a small space near the college. Q. Students soon began to visit it for both new and second-hand books. R. Ramesh had always dreamed of owning a bookshop. S. Today, the shop is a popular meeting place for readers in the town.
explanation: The opener and connectors fix this order.

question: Rearrange the sentences P, Q, R, S to form a meaningful paragraph: P. If the score is high, the loan is usually approved quickly. Q. A credit score is a number that reflects a person's creditworthiness. R. Therefore, maintaining a good score helps one get loans at lower interest rates. S. Banks check this score before approving a loan.
explanation: The opener and connectors fix this order.

question: Rearrange the sentences P, Q, R, S to form a meaningful paragraph: P. Doctors therefore advise switching off phones at least an hour before bed. Q. Yet many young people sleep less than six hours a night because of late-night screen use. R. During sleep, the body repairs tissues and the brain stores memories. S. Sleep is essential for good health.
explanation: The opener and connectors fix this order.

question: Rearrange the sentences P, Q, R, S to form a meaningful paragraph: P. Meena opened a small tailoring shop in her village with a loan from a self-help group. Q. Within two years, she had repaid the loan and hired three assistants. R. However, her neat work and fair prices slowly won people's trust. S. At first, she had very few customers.
explanation: The opener and connectors fix this order.

question: Rearrange the sentences P, Q, R, S to form a meaningful paragraph: P. Thus, a family can avoid sudden hardship after an accident or illness. Q. Insurance is a way of protecting oneself against financial loss. R. The insured person pays a small amount, called a premium, at regular intervals. S. In return, the insurer agrees to compensate for losses covered by the policy.
explanation: The opener and connectors fix this order.

question: Rearrange the sentences P, Q, R, S to form a meaningful paragraph: P. Regular practice is known to reduce stress and improve flexibility. Q. It combines physical postures, breathing exercises and meditation. R. That is why June 21 is now celebrated worldwide as International Yoga Day. S. Yoga originated in ancient India thousands of years ago.
explanation: The opener and connectors fix this order.

question: Rearrange the sentences P, Q, R, S to form a meaningful paragraph: P. Once the OTP is shared, money is withdrawn from the account within minutes. Q. Banks therefore remind customers never to disclose such details to anyone. R. Cases of online banking fraud have risen sharply in recent years. S. Fraudsters often pose as bank officials and ask customers for their OTP.
explanation: The opener and connectors fix this order.

question: Rearrange the sentences P, Q, R, S to form a meaningful paragraph: P. Its wide branches gave shade to travellers and cattle alike. Q. An old banyan tree stood at the centre of the village. R. The villagers mourned its loss as if they had lost an elder. S. One summer, a storm uprooted it completely.
explanation: The opener and connectors fix this order.

question: Rearrange the sentences P, Q, R, S to form a meaningful paragraph: P. For decades, a large part of rural India had no access to a bank account. Q. Under the scheme, crores of zero-balance accounts were opened within months. R. To address this, the government launched the Jan Dhan Yojana in 2014. S. Financial inclusion means bringing banking services to every citizen.
explanation: The opener and connectors fix this order.

question: Rearrange the sentences P, Q, R, S to form a meaningful paragraph: P. India is facing a growing water crisis. Q. If adopted widely, it could ease shortages in both cities and villages. R. Groundwater levels are falling in many states because of over-extraction. S. Rainwater harvesting can help recharge these aquifers.
explanation: The opener and connectors fix this order.

question: Rearrange the sentences P, Q, R, S to form a meaningful paragraph: P. He then practised mock tests daily for six months. Q. Instead of losing heart, he analysed where he had gone wrong. R. Arjun failed the bank exam on his first attempt. S. In his second attempt, he cleared the exam with a high rank.
explanation: The opener and connectors fix this order.

question: Rearrange the sentences P, Q, R, S to form a meaningful paragraph: P. Expanding this network is essential for their wider adoption. Q. Electric vehicles are gaining popularity in Indian cities. R. However, the lack of charging stations remains a major hurdle. S. They produce no tailpipe emissions and are cheaper to run.
explanation: The opener and connectors fix this order.

question: Rearrange the sentences P, Q, R, S to form a meaningful paragraph: P. Her dedication caught the attention of the state selectors. Q. Last year, she was chosen to represent India at the junior level. R. She trained every morning before school, even in the cold winter. S. Kavya joined the district hockey team at the age of twelve.
explanation: The opener and connectors fix this order.

question: Rearrange the sentences P, Q, R, S to form a meaningful paragraph: P. She explained that her debit card had been blocked by mistake. Q. Within minutes, the card was reactivated and she left smiling. R. A customer walked into the branch looking worried. S. The officer listened patiently and checked her account details.
explanation: The opener and connectors fix this order.

question: Rearrange the sentences P, Q, R, S to form a meaningful paragraph: P. India has emerged as one of the largest startup hubs in the world. Q. Young entrepreneurs are building companies in areas such as fintech and health care. R. As a result, these firms are creating lakhs of new jobs. S. Their growth has been supported by easy funding and digital infrastructure.
explanation: The opener and connectors fix this order.
